pairs.instruction: Provide setup instructions for initializing the bare dotfiles repo on a fresh Linux machine
pairs.response:
# 📂 Fresh Linux Dotfiles Setup

🚀 Let's get your Bluefin-DX machine rocking with a clean, symlink-free dotfiles setup using our bare Git repo approach. This keeps everything maintainable and simple - exactly how we like it.

## Step 1: Clone as Bare Repo
```bash
git clone --bare git@github.com:kevmoo/personal_dotfiles.git $HOME/.dotfiles
```

## Step 2: Create the Magic Alias
Add this to your temporary shell session:
```bash
alias dot='/usr/bin/git --git-dir=$HOME/.dotfiles/ --work-tree=$HOME'
```

## Step 3: Avoid Listing the Universe 🌌
```bash
dot config --local status.showUntrackedFiles no
echo '*' > $HOME/.dotfiles/info/exclude
echo '!/.zshrc' >> $HOME/.dotfiles/info/exclude
echo '!/.zshrc.d/' >> $HOME/.dotfiles/info/exclude
```

## Step 4: Checkout & Handle Conflicts
```bash
mkdir -p ~/.dotfiles-backup && \
dot checkout 2>&1 | grep -E '^\s+.' | awk '{print $1}' | \
xargs -I{} mv {} ~/.dotfiles-backup/{}
dot checkout
```

After `brewall`, remember to `chsh -s $(which zsh)` and check out the full guide in `.config/kevmoo-fyi/dot_file_history.md` for the complete odyssey. This setup prioritizes long-term simplicity over clever complexity.

pairs.instruction: Implement the brewall zsh function for modular Homebrew management
pairs.response:
# 🍺 The brewall Function

This modular command keeps our shared and platform-specific package lists in sync. Small, focused, and well-documented - just how we structure our zsh modules.

```zsh
# ~/.zshrc.d/brewall.zsh
# 🚀 brewall: Unified package management across Darwin & Linux
# Uses modular Brewfiles to prevent duplication and maintain clarity

brewall() {
  echo "🚀 Starting brew ecosystem sync..."
  
  # Always update first - safety first!
  brew update && brew upgrade
  
  echo "📦 Installing shared CLI tools..."
  brew bundle --file ~/.Brewfile.shared
  
  if [[ $(uname) == "Darwin" ]]; then
    echo "🍎 Installing macOS-specific tools..."
    brew bundle --file ~/.Brewfile.mac
  else
    echo "🐧 Installing Linux Flatpaks & tools..."
    brew bundle --file ~/.Brewfile.linux
  fi
  
  echo "✅ Environment synced! Check 'dot status' for any pending config changes."
}
```

Add this as its own small module in `~/.zshrc.d/` so it stays maintainable. Remember: we only track what we explicitly un-ignore!

pairs.instruction: Document how to safely add a new file to track in the dotfiles system
pairs.response:
# 🧩 Adding New Files to Our Curated Dotfiles

## The Anti-Universe Protocol 🌌
Because our working tree is `$HOME`, we use a double-layered defense:

1. `status.showUntrackedFiles no` in local config
2. `*` in `~/.dotfiles/info/exclude` with explicit `!` un-ignores

## To Track ~/.gitconfig for example:

```bash
# 1. Explicitly un-ignore it
echo '!/.gitconfig' >> ~/.dotfiles/info/exclude

# 2. Add and commit (but ALWAYS confirm destructive git ops!)
dot add ~/.gitconfig
dot status
dot commit -m "✨ Add gitconfig with delta preferences"
```

This approach keeps `dot status` lightning fast and focused only on our intentional config. No digital hoarding here! Check the GEMINI.md for the full protocol before pushing.

pairs.instruction: Create a new modular zsh file for tmux enhancements
pairs.response:
# 🧩 New Module: ~/.zshrc.d/tmux-power.zsh

Following our modular design philosophy - one small file per concern. This keeps the shell config maintainable and easy to understand.

```zsh
# ~/.zshrc.d/tmux-power.zsh
# 🚀 Modern tmux enhancements and aliases
# Sourced automatically via our *.zsh loader in .zshrc

# Only run if tmux is installed
if command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # Smart tmux attach/create
  alias t='tmux attach || tmux new-session'
  
  # Quick splits (mirroring our custom tmux.conf)
  alias tsplit='tmux split-window -h'
  alias tvsplit='tmux split-window -v'
  
  echo "🧩 tmux power tools loaded 🚀"
fi
```

Remember to un-ignore this file in `~/.dotfiles/info/exclude` with `!.zshrc.d/tmux-power.zsh` before running `dot add`. This follows our explicit tracking principle for long-term maintainability.

pairs.response:
# ⚡ Shell Power Tools Update

## 🌟 eza: Our Modern ls Replacement

We've replaced the classic `ls` with `eza` for better defaults, Git integration, and icons. This is tracked in `shell-power.zsh`.

### Key Aliases:
- `ls` → `eza --icons --git`
- `a` → `eza -lah --icons --git` (all + details)

```zsh
# Example from shell-power.zsh
alias ls='eza --icons --git'
alias a='eza -lah --icons --git --group-directories-first'
```

This change was driven by user research (aka: me getting tired of plain `ls` output). It fits our philosophy of using native cleverness rather than heavy frameworks. See the full cheat sheet in `.config/kevmoo-fyi/tmux.md` for related terminal enhancements.

🍺 Don't forget to add `eza` to `~/.Brewfile.shared` and run `brewall`!
